AUTHOR: Dawkins
TITLE: FishTrack23: An Ensemble Underwater Dataset for Multi-Object Tracking
VENUE: 2024 IEEE/CVF WINTER CONFERENCE ON APPLICATIONS OF COMPUTER VISION, WACV 2024
REGION: Bay of Biscay (France), northern Gulf of Mexico, Lake Jennings (California), main Hawaiian islands (USA)
SPECIES: ~200 species labels (e.g., red snapper, Deep 7 bottomfish, black seabream, largemouth bass); detectors trained on single 'fish' class
DATA: FishTrack23 ensemble: Ifremer DropCam, Game of Trawls, SEAMAP Reef Fish Video Survey, CDFW Habitat Monitoring, NOAA MOUSS
V_EV: Sec. 2.1: 'Due to turbidity, fish may come in and out of visibility'; Sec. 2.3.3: 'Data is typically collected at depths ranging from 15-200 m.'
D2: recommended train/test 23k/3.5k tracks; videos manually selected
D_EV: Sec. 2.2: 'Videos were manually selected to generate this split, ensuring that both a range of difficulties and multiple locations were included in the test set.'
R_EV: Sec. 4: 'the same detection approach was used in each method (CRCNN-MS) and evaluated on the test set' of the same FishTrack23 ensemble
C_EV: Sec. 3: 'exceed a fixed detection score (default=0.5)... A secondary pruning step compares overlaps on top of entire tracks to reduce duplicates.'
E_EV: Table 1 'Preliminary Algorithm Comparisons': only mAP, IDF1 and MCC reported
ARCH: Cascade R-CNN (CRCNN, multi-scale, motion variants); trackers TUT, SiamMask-MOT, ByteTrack; classifiers ResNeXt101, EfficientNetV2 with track averaging
NOTE: Video-level manually curated train/test split across a multi-programme ensemble; test includes multiple locations also present in training, so no external test. C5 credited for explicit duplicate-handling mechanisms (cross-tile NMS, track-overlap pruning to reduce duplicates) plus a stated default score threshold 0.5 (SM-MOT) -> C_ALL Y mechanically, although duplicates are not quantified and threshold is a default. Headline tracker (BYTE) is threshold-agnostic. NCLASS ~200 species (approximate) left null.
